snippet.title: Mosquitoes, Grilled Meat & Brain Freeze: Everyday Myths Put to the Test | Myth or Science (1/6)
snippet.description:
In Episode 1 of Myth or Science, microbiologist Dr Jennifer Gardy takes on some of the most common health and science claims we hear every day. Using her own body as part of the experiment, she travels from Florida’s mosquito labs to freezing cold research chambers, New York food tests, and a classroom ice cream challenge to separate fact from fiction.

Can mosquitoes really prefer women over men? Does grilled meat increase cancer risk? Does alcohol actually warm you up in cold weather? Do we lose most of our body heat through our head? Can eating too fast make you gain weight? And can brain freeze happen even on a cold day?

With humor, curiosity, and unorthodox experiments, Gardy puts each claim under the microscope, revealing the surprising science behind the myths that shape our everyday choices.

snippet.title: Alaska's Endless Winter | Freshly Milled Flour, Planting Our Garlic & More Snow
snippet.description:
March 20th 2026 - April 25th 2026

When spring isn't in the air we take action and get our outdoor raised beds ready for planting garlic. After attempting to clear the future wood shed site there's more repairs and maintenance to be done along with starting seeds and transplanting in the seed room. 

We try our hand at milling wheat berries comparing a stone burr mill to a modern high impact mill. The reward - nutritious, freshly milled flour for all our cooking and baking needs including delicious sourdough loaves.

Between homecooked meals, our furry friends, the chickens and picking up bees there's never a dull moment around here. After all the work is done we hit the road headed for Canada. 

We appreciate you tagging along for our Alaskan adventure 😀

Thank you for watching and supporting our channel! 💙
- Eric & Arielle

localized.description:
March 20th 2026 - April 25th 2026

When spring isn't in the air we take action and get our outdoor raised beds ready for planting garlic. After attempting to clear the future wood shed site there's more repairs and maintenance to be done along with starting seeds and transplanting in the seed room. 

We try our hand at milling wheat berries comparing a stone burr mill to a modern high impact mill. The reward - nutritious, freshly milled flour for all our cooking and baking needs including delicious sourdough loaves.

Between homecooked meals, our furry friends, the chickens and picking up bees there's never a dull moment around here. After all the work is done we hit the road headed for Canada. 

We appreciate you tagging along for our Alaskan adventure 😀

It's a full day event - setting up the barrel, limbing trees and spreading scent. After one week we are disappointed to find no bears have passed though the site but we remain optimistic they will come!

We appreciate you tagging along for our Alaskan adventure 😀

Thank you for watching and supporting our channel! 💙
- Eric & Arielle

snippet.title: How to make birch tar for survival #bushcraft #primitiveskills #survival
snippet.description:
Turning birch bark into birch tar — the old way.
Out in the snowy woods, I peeled fresh birch bark, shaved it fine, and rendered it down slow over a hot fire in a tin can for hours. The result? Thick, glossy, natural tar — one of the most useful things you can make in the bush.
Waterproofing, glue, medicine, fire starter… birch tar has been used for thousands of years. Nothing beats learning these primal skills.

snippet.title: Stop Using Staples? This Test Changes Everything
snippet.description:
Are fence staples actually holding your fence… or slowly failing?
We put them head-to-head against a modern fencing clip under real load.

In this video, we test a traditional barbed fencing staple against the Davos fencing clip using a controlled load test rig. By applying increasing pressure to both systems, we find out exactly how they fail — and which one holds stronger under real strain.

This matters because most staple failures don’t happen instantly — they loosen over time. If you’re building fences that need to last, understanding holding power, installation method, and long-term reliability is critical.

This video is for farmers, fencing contractors, and property owners who want stronger, faster, and more reliable fencing systems — without guesswork.

What you’ll see:

Real load testing using a calibrated strain rig
How staples actually fail in timber posts
Clip performance under extreme tension
Practical implications for real-world fencing

Key takeaway:
The staple failed at ~240kg.
The fencing clip held beyond ~435kg — and the post failed first.

This video explores fence construction methods, staple vs clip performance, fencing durability, load testing, tensile strength in fencing systems, and long-term fence reliability. It covers practical fencing techniques, how staples fail over time, and why modern fencing clips are being adopted by contractors and farmers looking for stronger and more efficient solutions.

When spring returns in Alaska we make good use of the warmer weather and longer daylight hours. After returning from a quick trip to Canada for our new SpaceKap, we get the garden planted early and head out on the boat for the first excursion of the season. 

This is also the time of year to use up the last of our produce stored in the crawlspace and make more room in the freezer. Teriyaki Caribou jerky goes onto the smoker between outings on the atv and tending to the garden. We fire up the barrel stove in the greenhouse for the first time and it proved to be well worth its weight in gold for protecting the plants from late season frosts.

snippet.title: Why Paddocks Stop Holding Water
snippet.description:
Most dry paddocks don’t just need more rain — they need to hold the rain they already get.
In this paddock discussion, Phil and Stuart explain why damaged soil sheds water, loses resilience, and stops supporting healthy plant growth.

Filmed in Victoria, this conversation looks at what happens when hard-setting soil, low organic matter, poor aggregation, overgrazing, bare ground and broken water cycles combine. The discussion moves from runoff and infiltration to soil carbon, fungi, plant cover, small water cycles, paddock recovery and the simple signs farmers can read in their own landscapes.

This video is useful for farmers, graziers, land managers and anyone interested in regenerative agriculture, paddock renovation, soil health, drought resilience and practical land restoration.

Phil's book https://www.groundbreakingpress.com/
Tarwyn Park Training https://www.tarwynparktraining.com.au/

Healthy soil, water infiltration, organic matter, soil aggregation, plant available water, pasture recovery, regenerative grazing, small water cycle, ground cover, fungi, carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, paddock renovation and drought resilience are all part of the same system. When the soil starts functioning again, rainfall becomes more effective.

Subscribe to Farm Learning with Tim Thompson for practical farming stories, soil health insights and real-world regenerative agriculture conversations.
Watch related videos on pasture recovery, soil biology, grazing management and water in the landscape.
If this helps explain a paddock you know, share it with someone working on land recovery.

Featured guests: Phil and Stuart
Topics: soil health, paddock renovation, water infiltration, regenerative grazing, small water cycle

snippet.title: Prisoners prepare for release and worry about an uncertain future | Inside The Women's Prison (3/3)
snippet.description:
As freedom looms for some and time stretches for others, one question lingers in the minds of the inmates in Institution A4 – will I be accepted? 

In this final episode of a three-part series, the women confront an uncertain future and potential rejection by their families, society and even themselves. Christeen, serving a life sentence, knows an upcoming review could change her fate but tensions with her cellmates mount. As Halen dreams of a future with a fiancé she has never met in person, Haziqah clings to the hope of reconnecting with her family during a long-awaited visit. For Joanna and Yuxin, the end of their sentences is within reach but their paths to freedom are far from clear. Joanna struggles with the possibilities of being abandoned by family and friends, while Yu Xin, determined to maintain her sobriety, faces her own challenge: her first job interview in years. 

------

Women make up about 10% of Singapore’s prison population. And inside the walls of Institution A4, at the Changi Prison Complex, are about 800 female inmates, incarcerated for various offences.

snippet.description:
I tested ZoupW 450W “shade tolerant” solar panels in real off-grid conditions at my cabin.

In this video, I compare them against a standard solar setup in full sun, partial shade, and heavy shade, then use them to power the cabin over a full weekend with an EcoFlow Delta Max 2.

Are they actually better in shade - or is it mostly marketing?
